subject: forensic-medicine
title: Cocaine: Excitement, Depression, Crack and Cocaine Bugs

steps.title: Cocaine from coca leaves
steps.tx: **Cocaine** comes from leaves of Erythroxylum coca holding nought point five to one percent alkaloid, a colourless odourless crystalline substance of bitter taste, street names coke, snow, cadillac and white lady. Crack is cocaine combined with baking soda and water for smoking. It desensitises terminal nerves and vasoconstricts locally, its legitimate use as local anaesthetic, and powerfully stimulates the central nervous system briefly then depresses it, releasing dopamine and serotonin in the pleasure centre with sympathomimetic effect like amphetamine.
steps.say: Coca leaf crystals that numb, constrict and then intoxicate through dopamine are cocaine, and crack is its smokable form.

steps.title: Speed of onset by route
steps.tx: **Cocaine onset follows its route**: inhaled in one to three minutes, intravenous or smoked in seconds peaking at three to five minutes, topical nasal mucosa peaking at twenty to thirty minutes, oral peaking at sixty to ninety minutes. Action is so short that a high needs redosing every half to one hour. It is hydrolysed by liver and plasma esterases to ecgonine methyl ester and benzoylecgonine, biological half life half to one hour, appearing almost immediately in urine and cleared within twenty four hours.
steps.say: Seconds by vein or smoke, half an hour by nose and an hour by mouth, gone within a day: cocaine's clock is its route.

nodes.label: Peak in seconds to ninety minutes
High fades, redose in an hour

steps.title: Stage of excitement
steps.tx: The **excitement stage** brings bitter taste, dry mouth, dysphagia, well being with loss of depression and fatigue, then excitement, restlessness and talkativeness passing into calm dullness. Pulse and respirations are rapid and deep, pupils dilated, headache, pallor, cyanosis, sweating and raised temperature appear, reflexes are exaggerated with tremors or convulsions, and hallucinations with mania may supervene. Tingling in hands and feet and numbness where the drug touched, nose and throat after sniffing, are characteristic local signatures.
steps.say: Talkative, flushed hot, wide pupilled and tremulous with a numb nose: cocaine excitement mimics a sympathomimetic storm.

steps.tx: A septal perforation marks the nose that cocaine has touched. Numbness there, and in the throat, plus tingling in the hands and feet, is the local signature of sniffing. The **excitement stage** then brings a bitter taste, dry mouth and dysphagia, wellbeing with loss of depression and fatigue, then restlessness and talkativeness that pass into calm dullness. Pulse and breathing run rapid and deep, pupils dilate, and pallor, cyanosis, sweating and fever appear, with tremor, convulsions or mania.
steps.say: Sniffed cocaine numbs the nose and throat and tingles in the hands and feet, and a septal hole is the chronic local injury. Excitement brings a bitter taste, dry mouth, restless talk, then dull calm. Pulse and breathing race, pupils widen, and tremor, convulsions or hallucinations can follow.

vis.caption: The nasal septum has a clean perforation where chronic sniffing has destroyed the cartilage. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Stage of depression and sudden death
steps.tx: Within an hour or less the **depression stage** follows: feeble respirations, profuse perspiration, collapse, convulsions and death from respiratory failure, cardiac failure or vascular collapse. Sudden death follows intravenous injection and smoking more than snorting, from cardiac arrhythmias by direct myocardial action and cardiopulmonary arrest. Cocaine hypertension can burst a cerebral vessel or aneurysm and cause coronary spasm; a person may die suddenly during or immediately after a struggle, the excited delirium death that demands careful autopsy.
steps.say: Collapse within the hour, arrhythmia after vein or smoke, and death in a struggle are cocaine's killing patterns.

steps.title: Cocaine complications across organs
steps.tx: **Cocaine complications** read like a vascular catalogue: cerebrovascular accidents, subarachnoid and intracerebral haemorrhage, myocardial infarction, skin necrosis, aortic dissection and pulmonary infarcts. Chronic snorting perforates the nasal septum. The heart at autopsy may show foci of scarring that source fatal dysrhythmias, and lungs weigh three to four times normal with congestion and oedema after fatal use. Cocaine with heroin injected together is the speedball, and death under alcohol's influence compounds forensic interpretation.
steps.say: Infarcts, dissections, haemorrhages and a scarred irritable heart are the organs' record of cocaine's vascular violence.

steps.title: Formication: the cocaine bugs
steps.tx: Chronic cocaine use produces **Magnan sign or cocaine bugs**, a tactile hallucination of insects crawling under the skin, classically grouped with alcoholic formication in delirium tremens. The user scratches and excoriates the skin hunting the insects, leaving patterned self inflicted lesions that can imitate assault or infestation. Combined with paranoia and panic on large doses or binges, anxiety leading to paranoia, the mental picture separates stimulant psychosis from primary schizophrenia by its drug timeline and autonomic storm.
steps.say: Insects felt crawling under cocaine skin are hallucinated, and the scratch marks they provoke must not be read as assault.

steps.tx: Chronic cocaine use produces the **Magnan sign**, or cocaine bugs, a tactile hallucination of insects crawling under the skin, grouped classically with formication in alcoholic delirium tremens. Scratching to catch those insects leaves patterned, self inflicted excoriations that imitate assault or a real infestation. Large doses and binges add panic and paranoia. The drug timeline plus the autonomic storm is what separates this stimulant picture from primary schizophrenia.
steps.say: Cocaine bugs, the Magnan sign, are insects felt crawling under the skin, the same formication as in delirium tremens. Scratching leaves patterned marks that can be mistaken for assault or infestation. A drug timeline and an autonomic storm separate this state from primary schizophrenia.

steps.title: Treatment and the antidote tradition
steps.tx: **Cocaine treatment** is decontamination and stabilisation: gastric lavage with warm water, permanganate, charcoal or tannic acid after oral intake, washing drug off nose and throat, a ligature above an injected part in the classical regimen, convulsions controlled with short acting barbiturates in Reddy's text and benzodiazepines in modern practice, amyl nitrite inhalation as the traditional antidote, airway and circulatory stabilisation, thiamine one hundred milligrams intravenously and naloxone two milligrams where opioid co ingestion is possible in speedball deaths.
steps.say: Wash it out, sedate the convulsions, stabilise heart and airway, and remember naloxone when a speedball partner may be aboard.

steps.title: Preserving cocaine evidence before it vanishes
steps.tx: **Cocaine decomposes rapidly**, so blood is preserved with fluoride to stop esterase hydrolysis, and brain is analysed because it does not hydrolyse cocaine to benzoylecgonine as blood does. Cocaine, amphetamine, nicotine and barbiturates can be found in the stomach even when given parenterally. Nasal swabs, the powder, straws and pipes, and urine taken immediately carry the case. A negative blood cocaine after delay is meaningless without the metabolite and brain results beside it.
steps.say: Fluoride in the blood tube and brain on the bench rescue a cocaine case that plain delayed blood would silently lose.

steps.title: Stimulant toxidrome at the bedside
steps.tx: Cocaine anchors the **sympathomimetic toxidrome** met in the general toxicology module: dilated pupils, tachycardia, hypertension, hyperthermia, sweating, agitation and convulsions. The differential runs through amphetamine, which lasts longer, anticholinergic poisoning, which is dry rather than sweaty, and thyrotoxicosis and phaeochromocytoma medically. Sweating with wide pupils and a racing heart after a powder or pipe is stimulant poisoning until excluded, and cooling plus sedation precede any specific drug history.
steps.say: Sweaty, wide pupilled, hot and racing is the stimulant storm; cool and sedate first and take the drug history second.
